biomarkers.name: SF3B1 mutation
biomarkers.prevalence: ~60-90% of MDS with ring sideroblasts / SF3B1-associated cases
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defining feature in modern classification; associated with relatively favourable prognosis. WHO 2022 recognises 'MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation' as a distinct entity; ring sideroblasts are not required when SF3B1 mutation is present

biomarkers.name: Ring sideroblasts (Perls stain, ≥15% or ≥5% with SF3B1)
Luspatercept response
biomarkers.clinical_use: Luspatercept (activin receptor ligand trap) is approved for anemia in lower-risk MDS with ring sideroblasts after ESA failure and, based on COMMANDS, also approved in some settings as first-line therapy for transfusion-dependent lower-risk MDS

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Erythroid dysplasia with ring sideroblasts (≥15% of erythroid precursors, or ≥5% if SF3B1-mutant) on Perls iron stain — iron granules in mitochondria around erythroblast nucleus
variants: WHO 2022: 'MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation' (SF3B1-defined entity)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Generally favourable risk relative to many other MDS subtypes, though risk depends on overall IPSS-R/IPSS-M and co-mutations

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Not the paradigm; ineffective erythropoiesis is the pathophysiologic problem
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Ring sideroblasts pathognomonic (iron-loaded mitochondria around erythroblast nucleus)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: HSC with SF3B1 mutation causing distinctive splicing-driven dysregulation of erythroid differentiation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Erythroid dysplasia with distinctive ring sideroblasts (≥15% of erythroid precursors, or ≥5% if SF3B1-mutant) — iron-loaded mitochondria around erythroblast nucleus indicating ineffective erythropoiesis with mitochondrial iron mishandling
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: SF3B1 splicing factor mutation reshapes RNA splicing programme; altered splicing of genes involved in mitochondrial function and heme/iron handling contributes to mitochondrial iron accumulation and ring sideroblast formation
